items.title: Isaiah "Ike" Robinson Interview, 1961-04-28
items.q: I think I got with Ernest Milton on about 34. 33 or 34. Yeah, I was playing with Milton. We played together about three or four years.

ctx.x: With Chris's band then? Was he the leader?

Yeah, he'd be the leader but we'd pick up men, you see. Pick up anybody? Anybody. That's how I would. He'd pick up like the guy well known if he'd get killed or die. Well, they had fellas going around, one by the name, Ernest, French, Taki, or Jerry. Well, they'd go around and pick up. What's the name of they'd pick up? He'd carry to Chris and we'd play a few.
Yeah. Those guys would be like agents for Chris, would they? Picking up the work?

items.title: Isaiah "Ike" Robinson Interview, 1961-04-28
items.q: Watch told me, he said, well, you men, you got a dollar man, you got five, now I can take six bits.

ctx.x: Yeah, Buddy Petit was dead then.

Yeah. Yeah. About 33 or 34, I started playing with Milton. We played together about three or four years. Oh. And that's, that run out. Music was absolutely nothing. You got around, when you getting down playing music, you got a man to change a dollar and play, and you know that was tough. Yeah. I remember once, I got a little job there for this lottery man there on Hawks, that jury man on Stephen All Street. He had a little dance at a, you know, had a band that come play there for his lottery. I think I charged…
Well, you didn't even save your heart then? No.
